reason: The Moon’s unequal pull across Earth is the natural starting point for tides.

expectation: This should reveal the difference in the Moon’s pull across Earth.

effect: The Moon’s uneven pull is now available as the basis for the tidal sequence.

reason: Raised rims can trap water in rock hollows as the tide falls.

reaction: It was satisfying to see why the hollows had to fill before they could retain pools.

mostWorthwhile.text: Following the tide into shallow coastal water was worthwhile: it showed how local seabed and coastline shape the response, rather than lunar distance alone.

leastWorthwhile.text: Trying to combine the exposed beach with the hollows was least worthwhile: the beach had no available combination, so I had to find another route.

surprise.text: I was surprised that the hollows needed the coastal tide itself to fill them first, rather than combining directly with the exposed beach.

arbitrary.text: The failed beach-and-hollows pairing felt unintuitive at first, though the subsequent filling step gave it a clear physical purpose.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to follow more natural processes, especially where the combinations clarify how familiar features form.
